```{r, load libraries}
#| output: FALSE

#Loading required libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(psych)
library(gt)
library(janitor)
```

```{r, load data}
#| output: FALSE

#Reading data file

data <- read_excel("./Attachment_Anxiety_Data.xlsx")


```

```{r, clean data}
#| output: FALSE

#Assign informative labels to Gender, Relationship, and Ethnicity variables
#Select to keep only gender, relationship and ethnicity columns, as well as columns containing questionnaire items
#Mutate to convert scores to integers

data.clean <- data |>
  mutate(Gender = case_when(Gender == 1 ~ "Male", Gender == 2 ~ "Female", TRUE ~ NA)) |>
  mutate(Relationship = case_when(Relationship == 1 ~ "married", 
                                  Relationship == 2 ~ "in a relationship",
                                  Relationship == 4 ~ "divorced",
                                  Relationship == 5 ~ "in a relationship",
                                  Relationship == 6 ~ "never been in a relationship",
                                  Relationship == 7 ~ "prefer not to say")) |>
  mutate(Ethnicity = case_when(Ethnicity == 1 ~ "white/Caucasian",
                               Ethnicity == 2 ~ "Asian/Asian British",
                               Ethnicity == 3 ~ "Other ethnic group",
                               Ethnicity == 4 ~ "prefer not to say")) |>
  select(Gender, Relationship,Ethnicity, SA_1:SEst_10) |>
    mutate(across(SA_1:SEst_10, as.integer))

```

```{r, score items}
#| output: FALSE

#Creating answer keys that list which items belong to each subscale
#"-" designates reverse-keyed items

#Social Anxiety
key_SA <- list(`Social Anxiety` = c("SA_1","SA_2","SA_3","SA_4","-SA_5","SA_6","SA_7","SA_8","-SA_9","SA_10","-SA_11","SA_12","SA_13","SA_14","SA_15","SA_16","SA_17","SA_18","SA_19","SA_20"))

#Attachment-Related Anxiety
key_AA <- list(`Attachment-Related Anxiety` = c("AA_1","AA_2","AA_3","AA_4","AA_5","AA_6","AA_7","AA_8","AA_9"))

#Self-Esteem
key_SE <- list(`Self-Esteem` = c("SEst_1","-SEst_2","SEst_3","SEst_4","-SEst_5","-SEst_6","SEst_7","-SEst_8","-SEst_9","SEst_10"))

#Computing average scores for each person & Cronbach's alpha
#State minimum and maximum value for each subscale
#Save each new scores function as a data frame

#Social Anxiety
scores_SA<-scoreItems(key_SA, data.clean, totals = F, min=1, max=4)
scores_SA.df<-as.data.frame(scores_SA$scores)

#Attachment-Related Anxiety
scores_AA<-scoreItems(key_AA, data.clean, totals = F, min=1, max=7)
scores_AA.df<-as.data.frame(scores_AA$scores)

#Self-Esteem
scores_SE<-scoreItems(key_SE, data.clean, totals = F, min=1, max=4)
scores_SE.df<-as.data.frame(scores_SE$scores)
```

```{r, combine data frames}
#| output: FALSE

#Combine all score sets into a single dataframe
allscores.df <- cbind(scores_SA.df, scores_AA.df, scores_SE.df)

#combine scores dataframe with clean dataframe
data.clean<-cbind(data.clean, allscores.df)

```

```{r, reduced data}
#| output: FALSE

#Selecting the columns I'd like to appear in final tables

data.final <- data.clean |>
  select("Gender", "Relationship", "Ethnicity", "Social Anxiety", "Attachment-Related Anxiety", "Self-Esteem") |>
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)
```

```{r, reproducible table for relationship distribution}
#| output: FALSE

#Create demographic table of relationship status by gender
demographic.table <- data.final |>
  tabyl(Gender, Relationship)

#Create reproducible gt demographic table
#Rename column labels for proper casing 
demographic.gt.table <- demographic.table |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("*Distribution of Males and Females by Relationship*")
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    married = "Married",
    `in a relationship` = "In a relationship",
    divorced = "Divorced",
    `in a relationship` = "In a relationship",
    `never been in a relationship` = "Never been in a relationship",
    `prefer not to say` = "Prefer not to say"
  ) |>
  
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = everything()
  )

  
```  

```{r, reproducible table for anxiety scores}
#| output: FALSE

#Create summary statistics for columns of interest
summary <- describe(select(data.final, `Social Anxiety`:`Self-Esteem`))

#Get sample size
n <- (describe(data.final))[1,2]

#Create subscales object to appear in tables
Scales <- c("Social Anxiety", "Attachment-Related Anxiety", "Self-Esteem")

#Create new column called scales
summary$Scales<- Scales

#Calculate Cronbach's alpha for each subscale, round to 2 decimal places
alphas <- round(c(scores_SA$alpha,
                  scores_AA$alpha,
                  scores_SE$alpha),2)
  
#Select columns to appear in final table, round to 2 decimal places
summary <- summary |>
  select(Scales, mean, median, sd, range) |>
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

#Combine summary information with alpha values
final.summary <- cbind(summary, alphas)

#Create a reproducible table
summary.gt.table <- gt(final.summary) |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("*Descriptive Statistics for Social Anxiety, Attachment-Related Anxiety, and Self-Esteem*")
  ) 


  
```

```{r, filtered dataset}

#Filter the data for only participants who were in a relationship

data.filtered <- data.clean |>
  filter(Relationship == "in a relationship")
         
#Recalculate alpha values using filtered data, round to 2 decimal places

alphas_filtered <- (round(c(scores_SA$alpha,
                             scores_AA$alpha,
                             scores_SE$alpha),2))

#Create new summary statistics for filtered data
summary_filtered <- describe(select(data.filtered, `Social Anxiety`:`Self-Esteem`))

#Create subscales object to appear in tables
Scales <- c("Social Anxiety", "Attachment-Related Anxiety", "Self-Esteem")

#Create new column called scales
summary_filtered$Scales<- Scales

#Select columns to appear in final table, round values to 2 decimal places
summary_filtered <- summary_filtered |>
  select(Scales, mean, median, sd, range) |>
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

#combine new summary statistics with new alpha values
filtered.table <- cbind(summary_filtered, alphas_filtered)

#create new reproducible gt table for filtered data
filtered.gt.table <- gt(filtered.table) |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("*Descriptive Statistics for Social Anxiety, Attachment-Related Anxiety, and Self-Esteem for People in Relationships*")
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    alphas_filtered = "alphas")

```


## Intro

## Methods

### Participants

In this data set there were `{r} n` participants, with varying distributions of relationship status across gender (Table 1).

`{r} demographic.gt.table`

### Measures

This data set includes three subscales relating to attachment and social anxiety. Social Anxiety refers to the degree to which social anxiety plays a role in an individual's daily life (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[1]`). Attachment-Related Anxiety refers to the presence of anxiety and avoidance in adult relationships (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[2]`). Self-Esteem refers to a person's opinion of their own worth and abilities (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[3]`).

### Data Analysis Strategy

In the Social Anxiety subscale, the data for variables SA_5, SA_9, and SA_11 were reverse keyed. In the Self-Esteem subscale, the data for variables SEst_2, SEst_5, SEst_6, SEst_8, and SEst_9 were reverse keyed.

## Results

`{r} summary.gt.table`
This data set includes three subscales relating to attachment and social anxiety. Participants had a mean score on Social Anxiety of `r final.summary[1,2]`, on Attachment Related Anxiety of `r final.summary[2,2]`, and on Self-Esteem of `r final.summary[3,2]`.

`{r} filtered.gt.table`
This data set includes three subscales relating to attachment and social anxiety. When only including participants who were in a relationship, participants has a mean score on Social Anxiety of `r summary_filtered[1,2]`, on Attachment-Related Anxiety of `r summary_filtered[2,2]`, and on Self-Esteem of `r summary_filtered[3,2]`.
